_comment: Tesla Tools Suite Configuration - Copy this file to 'config.json' or 'resources/config.json' and customize your local paths. directories.archive is optional (null by default) - when omitted or null, archives automatically default to an 'archive' subfolder inside directories.data or the target JSON directory. If directories.external_drive is null/omitted, drives matching /Volumes/TESLADRIVE* are auto-discovered. evnex.username/evnex.password are your normal Evnex app login (email + password) for the community-maintained `evnex` python library (https://github.com/hardbyte/python-evnex), which talks to Evnex's own consumer app API - Evnex only issues real API keys to Enterprise/CP-Link customers. Prefer the EVNEX_CLIENT_USERNAME/EVNEX_CLIENT_PASSWORD env vars over config.json if you'd rather not keep the password on disk at all. pv.provider selects the active Tools/providers_pv/ implementation (get_pv_provider(), default 'solaredge' if omitted) - solaredge.api_key/solaredge.site_id are the SolarEdge Monitoring API credentials it reads (see providers_pv/pv_solaredge.py). pvoutput.api_key/pvoutput.system_id are placeholders for the PVOutput.org API (see resources/PVOUTPUT_API.md) - REQ-140 (2026-09-25) found this account's own PVOutput setup was a pure relay of the SAME SolarEdge account's own API, not an independent source, so no script uses this block by default any more; lib/pvoutput_common.py's functions still work standalone if you want to query PVOutput directly for some other reason. power.provider selects the active Tools/providers_power/ implementation (get_power_provider(), default 'agl' if omitted). power.usage_staleness_days (REQ-071) is the age, in days, at which sync_power_usage.py's post-consolidate reminder starts nagging for a fresh usage-export CSV from a manual-sync provider like AGL (default 14 if omitted) - purely a reminder, never blocks anything. directories.power_invoices is optional (omit or null) - the folder where the active power provider's (AGL, currently the only one) raw invoice PDFs and manual usage-export CSVs live; if unset, invoice scanning/filing/consolidation for that provider simply finds nothing there and skips it gracefully - no default folder is guessed. osm.client_id/osm.client_secret are an OpenStreetMap OAuth2 app's credentials (register one at https://www.openstreetmap.org/oauth2/applications), used by places_osm_editor.py - leave osm out entirely if you don't use that tool. abrp.target_arrival_soc/abrp.max_charge_soc/abrp.corridor_radius_km are the persistent defaults for charger_find.py's --target-soc/--max-soc/--corridor-radius route-planning flags (target: minimum acceptable arrival battery %, default 10; max: charging target ceiling % to charge to at an enroute stop - not the departure SoC, which is --soc's own concern - default 80 here, since supercharging speed tapers hard past 80%; corridor_radius_km: max lateral highway detour in km, default 5.0) - each still overridable per-run via its CLI flag. REQ-150 (2026-09-27): the old 'solar' block (ROI-calculator figures) has moved out of config.json entirely into its own real data file, Solar/solar_system.json (a sibling of AGL/, PVOutput/, SolarEdge/ under directories.data) - see Solar/solar_system.example.json in the repo for its shape and lib/solar_system_config.py for the loader; config.json itself no longer has a 'solar' key at all.
